newsitem.title: JORDAN: Leading Israel Labour party figure in Jordan visit.
newsitem.headline: Leading Israel Labour party figure in Jordan visit.

text.p: A leading Israeli Labour party member, Ehud Barak, held talks on Sunday with Jordanian leaders on the Middle East peace process and bilateral ties, officials said.

Ehud Barak, a main contender for the leadership of the opposition Labour party, told reporters after a meeting with Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti that they discussed bilateral ties and ways of pushing ahead the peace process.
"We discussed the bilateral relationship with Jordan and the issues in the trilateral triangle, Israel Jordan and the Palestinians and the overall issues of the Middle East," Barak told reporters.
Officials said Barak was also expected to meet Crown Prince Hassan over lunch and later hold talks with King Hussein during a two-day visit to the country.
Barak said he saw "Jordan as a major contributor to the peace process and to the chances of having a Middle East which is stable, blooming and with a cooperative environment."
Barak also said he listened to what he termed "Jordanian sensitivity to the timing" of last week's Israeli government plan to boost Jewish settlements in Arab East Jerusalem.

King Hussein has urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to reconsider the decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel, a hill captured by Israeli forces in the 1967 Middle East war.
Jordan is concerned by the Jewish state's policy of expanding settlements in the West Bank, which Amman views as a direct threat to its security.
Amman also fears a collapse of the peace process could spark renewed violence in Palestinian areas that will reverberate in Jordan, where a large portion of the population are of Palestinian origin.
